item.title: Rikugien Garden — Guide
item.description: Rikugien, in Tokyo’s Bunkyo ward, is widely regarded as one of the city’s most beautiful traditional Japanese gardens. Completed in 1702, this Edo-period ‘strolling garden’ was designed to recreate in miniature 88 scenes from classical Japanese and Chinese poetry, laid out around a large central pond with small islands, wooded hills, winding paths, stone bridges and elegant teahouses. A leisurely circuit reveals ever-changing views, and you can pause at a teahouse for matcha and a sweet overlooking the water.

item.title: Ritsurin Garden: A Daimyo's Masterpiece — Guide
item.description: Ritsurin Garden in Takamatsu is widely considered one of the finest gardens in Japan, a masterpiece of the strolling-garden style created over generations by the daimyo lords of the region. Larger and, many argue, lovelier than the famous ‘three great gardens’, it unfolds over a vast area of six ponds and thirteen landscaped hills, backed by the wooded slope of Mount Shiun as ‘borrowed scenery’. Winding paths lead across arched bridges, past pruned pines, teahouses and stone lanterns, each turn composing a new picture.

item.title: Suizenji Garden — Guide
item.description: Suizenji Jōjuen, a beautiful traditional landscape garden in Kumamoto city, was begun in the seventeenth century by the ruling Hosokawa lords as a tea retreat. Designed as a ‘strolling garden’ around a large pond fed by clear spring water from Mount Aso, its most famous feature is a miniature recreation of the 53 post stations of the old Tōkaidō highway between Kyoto and Edo — including a distinctive grassy conical hill representing Mount Fuji — laid out along the walking path so that a stroll around the pond becomes a symbolic journey.

item.title: Tokachi Millennium Forest Guide: Gardens, Tickets & Access
item.description: In the rolling countryside of the Tokachi plain lies the Tokachi Millennium Forest, one of Japan’s most celebrated contemporary gardens. Conceived as a 1,000-year project to reconnect people with nature, it blends manicured garden artistry with the wild Hokkaido landscape — most famously the sculpted, wave-like grass mounds of the Earth Garden and the lush perennial borders of the Meadow Garden, designed by acclaimed plantsman Piet Oudolf. An international garden-design award-winner, it’s a serene, beautiful stop, with goats, cafés, cycling and forest trails to enjoy at a gentle pace.
